learningOutcomes: Define implied volatility and verify that put-call parity requires identical implied volatility for calls and puts at the same strike and maturity ([fact-01], [fact-02]).
Differentiate the symmetric U-shaped currency volatility smile from the downward-sloping equity volatility skew ([fact-03], [fact-04]).
Explain the leverage effect and Hull's 'Crashophobia' (1987 crash impact) as drivers of equity volatility skew ([fact-05], [fact-06]).
Extract risk-neutral probability density functions using the Breeden-Litzenberger formula ([fact-07]).
Construct volatility surfaces $\sigma(K, T)$ and evaluate advanced stochastic and local volatility models (Dupire, Heston) ([fact-09], [fact-10], [fact-11]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: If Black-Scholes held perfectly in reality, implied volatility would be constant across all strikes and maturities; the empirical presence of smiles and skews proves actual market distributions depart from lognormality ([fact-01]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Put-call parity strictly dictates that European calls and puts sharing identical strike $K$ and maturity $T$ must have the exact same implied volatility to prevent synthetic arbitrage ([fact-02]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: As explained in Business Snapshot 19.2, equity volatility smiles were virtually flat prior to the October 19, 1987 market crash; institutional fear of catastrophic plunges ('Crashophobia') permanently steepened the equity skew post-crash ([fact-06]).

coreTakeaways: Implied volatility measures market pricing divergence from flat lognormal BSM assumptions, but put-call parity enforces equal implied volatility across calls and puts at identical strikes ([fact-01], [fact-02]).
Currency options form symmetric U-shaped smiles, whereas equities exhibit downward-sloping skews driven by leverage effects and post-1987 Crashophobia ([fact-03], [fact-04], [fact-05], [fact-06]).

Advanced quantitative finance utilizes Breeden-Litzenberger risk-neutral densities, 3D volatility surfaces $\sigma(K, T)$, Dupire local volatility, and Heston stochastic volatility models ([fact-07], [fact-09], [fact-11]).
